chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I made a vow for one of my sons that if Allah healed him, I would perform Hajj on foot. So I walked until I reached al-'Aqabah, then I complained [of fatigue] and rode. Then I found ease and walked again. I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said, 'I like that if you are wealthy, you slaughter a cow.' I said, 'I have expenses, and if I wished to slaughter [one], I would do so, and I have a debt.' He said, 'I like that if you are wealthy, you slaughter a cow.' I said, 'Is it something obligatory that I do?' He said, 'No. Whoever dedicates something to Allah and reaches his capacity, there is nothing upon him [to do more].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fulfilling a vow to perform Hajj on foot if one finds it difficult?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the preferred method of fulfilling a vow and the absolute limit of obligation, emphasizing that once a person reaches their 'capacity' (juhd), no further burden is required. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that vows are binding but flexible, allowing for substitution or completion based on one's financial and physical means, rather than imposing undue hardship.
